findings.title: Permission is granted in another namespace
findings.cause: container watcher exits because the API server refuses its ServiceAccount app: it may not list configmaps in namespace default. RoleBinding app-settings-reader grants it, through Role settings-reader, in namespace kd-rbac-other-namespace only: a RoleBinding grants in its own namespace, and the request is for namespace default; its log says: "Error from server (Forbidden): configmaps is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-other-namespace:app\" cannot list resource \"configmaps\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"default\""; Deployment config-watcher has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container watcher exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 6 times
last lines of container watcher's log (run that exited)
evidence.detail: Error from server (Forbidden): configmaps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-other-namespace:app" cannot list resource "configmaps" in API group "" in the namespace "default"

evidence.what: Role settings-reader, bound by RoleBinding app-settings-reader: apiGroups [""], resources ["configmaps"], verbs ["get", "list", "watch"]
evidence.command: kubectl get role settings-reader -n kd-rbac-other-namespace -o jsonpath='{.rules}'

evidence.what: RoleBinding app-settings-reader grants Role settings-reader to ServiceAccount app

findings.fix: If the app should read namespace default, create a Role and a RoleBinding there for ServiceAccount kd-rbac-other-namespace/app; if it should read its own, correct the namespace it is configured with (it asks for default).
